descriptionChirho: To move part of the body back and forth as a physical gesture, specifically shaking or wagging the head in derision or mockery (Matt 27:39; Mark 15:29).
To cause physical movement or to be in motion; used of general movement including living and existing (Acts 17:28 'in him we live and move') and moving objects (Matt 23:4).
To cause social or emotional agitation, to incite or create a disturbance; used figuratively of stirring up trouble among people (Acts 24:5) or a city being thrown into commotion (Acts 21:30).
To move something from its established position, to remove or displace; used of removing a lampstand from its place (Rev 2:5) and mountains being moved from their positions (Rev 6:14).
